prior_importants.description: All five issue forms say the operator applies `ready` once the ticket passes intake, which reverses ADR 0176: `ready` is applied first (by the operator or a write-access collaborator) and intake then checks the fields and removes it on failure.

findings.description: The "Testable (docs)" example cites `pup session ask --option`, a command docs/02-cli.md never mentions, so a filer modelling a ticket on it names a nonexistent command as the checkable claim.
The proof example `pup status --json` uses a `--json` flag docs/02-cli.md does not document, so a chore filer could copy an unrunnable proof check.

The forms apply labels `feature`, `chore-refactor`, `docs-spike` and `follow-up`, which nothing in the repo creates; GitHub does not create missing labels from a form's `labels:` key, so issues filed from those forms carry no type label until the labels exist.

process_issues.description: Re-ask on an unchanged head (5f68aea). Gated roster same as round 1: context, conventions, docs. Skipped correctness and security (no logic or trust boundary: YAML issue forms and markdown only), simplicity (the new files are the deliverable), guards (no non-test source), workflow-safety (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, not .github/workflows), spec (no closing issue or --spec source), maintainability (off the default roster). Prior important 0 (`ready` order) is still present at bug.yml:10-11 and the other four forms. Dropped one context nit (no ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml, so blank issues stay possible) because the reviewer conceded intake still catches them, so nothing goes wrong.
